title: The High Current
premise: Quentin Coldharbour, a bush pilot who has spent seven years outrunning a past they refuse to name, discovers a tide-revealed cave holding the wreck of the Meridian Star—a lost mail plane carrying both treasure and letters that could rewrite the history of the coast's forgotten families. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet across six tides, Quentin is forced into an uneasy alliance with the coastal community they've kept at arm's length: an old lighthouse keeper who knew Quentin's missing father, and a teenage stowaway pilot named Wren. As the tides close in, Quentin learns the wreck's true inheritance isn't gold but memory—the last flight logs of their father—and must choose between selling the past to buy freedom or anchoring themselves to people for the first time. In the end, Quentin surrenders the salvage claim, keeps only the letters, and lands for good.
about_author: I. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic turned storyteller who grew up between coastal airstrips and her grandmother's archive of unsent letters. They write adventure fiction about people who measure their lives in distances until something forces them to count in years.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A routine medicine run over the grey interior establishes Quentin's solitary life measured in miles and their careful avoidance of attachments. The emotional beat is restless competence masking loneliness, ending when a low tide reveals a cave mouth no chart admits exists.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Quentin explores the cave on foot at ebb tide and finds the corroded tail of a mail plane, its registration half-legible. POV stays with Quentin; the beat is awe curdling into dread as they recognize the aircraft type their father once flew.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin reluctantly visits Ede Okonkwo, the retired lighthouse keeper, to ask about the wreck without revealing why. Ede recognizes Quentin's surname instantly. POV shifts to Ede, whose chapter carries grief and guarded hope—she has waited seven years for this question.

chapters.title: Rumors Travel Faster Than Planes
chapters.summary: Wren, a sixteen-year-old hangar rat, overhears Quentin radioing about the find and spreads it unintentionally through the coastal net. Quentin's POV; the beat is panic as the news reaches the ears of Voss, broker of the salvage fleet anchored two bays south.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Introduces the antagonist's cold arithmetic: wrecks are assets, coasts are inventory. He charts the tides and calculates he needs six days. The beat is quiet menace—he doesn't threaten; he schedules.

chapters.title: A Stowaway in the Cargo Bay
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers Wren hiding among supply crates mid-flight and can't turn back in weather. Forced conversation cracks Quentin's armor slightly. The beat is exasperation softening into reluctant responsibility—Quentin's first act of care in years.

chapters.title: Letters That Never Landed
chapters.summary: Ede shares her ledger: the Meridian Star carried undelivered mail from families scattered by a decades-old storm and scandal. Quentin realizes one bundle bears his father's handwriting. POV alternates; the beat is inheritance as burden rather than gift.

chapters.title: Tide Two
chapters.summary: First recovery dive attempt fails against current and silt; Quentin nearly drowns and is hauled out by Wren. POV Quentin. The beat is humiliation and gratitude tangled together—the body remembering it wants to live even when the heart hasn't decided.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Voss makes Quentin an offer: exclusive rights in exchange for coordinates, framed politely over shared whiskey. Quentin neither accepts nor refuses. POV Voss then Quentin; the beat is temptation—money enough to vanish forever, which is all Quentin ever wanted.

chapters.title: Hangar Nights
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: Wren teaches Quentin about the town's oral history while they patch the plane together; Ede cooks for three without being asked. POV Wren. The beat is found family assembling itself so gradually none of them notice.

chapters.title: The Chart Room
chapters.summary: Ede reveals old survey maps showing the cave was deliberately erased from records—to protect someone. Quentin suspects his father was involved. POV Ede. The beat is the past pressing its palm flat against the present.

chapters.title: Tide Four, Rising
chapters.summary: Salvage scouts arrive posing as fishermen; Wren spots their depth sounder and raises the alarm. A tense standoff on the water ends without violence but confirms the timeline has collapsed. POV Quentin. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Everything I Flew Away From
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter: why Quentin left seven years ago—a quarrel with his father the night before the Meridian Star's final flight. POV Quentin. The beat is guilt finally given language; the wreck may hold not treasure but an apology never delivered.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone drains Quentin's fuel and slashes a pontoon overnight. Suspicion fractures the alliance—did Wren talk? POV Wren, wounded by the accusation. Beat: trust tested precisely where it had begun to grow.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Confession
chapters.summary: The saboteur is revealed: a dockhand in Voss's pay, but also a man whose own family letter lies in the wreck. He defects, bringing Voss's tide schedule. POV dockhand (brief) then ensemble. Beat: enemies are just neighbors with worse options.

chapters.title: Five Tides Left, One Plane
chapters.summary: Race-against-time planning montage: the town commits boats, winches, and bodies to a recovery before Voss's barge arrives. POV rotates quickly. Beat: collective purpose replacing Quentin's solo calculus—the plan only works because Quentin finally asks for help.

chapters.title: Into the Cave
chapters.summary: The dive succeeds partially: the mail sacks are recovered, but the fuselage shifts and traps Wren. Quentin goes back in after them. POV Quentin underwater. Climax begins; beat: seven years of self-preservation spent in ninety seconds of courage.

chapters.title: The Last Flight Log
chapters.summary: Trapped by rising water, Quentin finds the cockpit and his father's logbook—final entries reveal the crash was deliberate, hiding the mail from men like Voss, and the last line is addressed to Quentin. Emotional peak: forgiveness arriving posthumously.

chapters.title: Out on the Ebb
chapters.summary: Extraction as the tide turns; Wren and Quentin surface together as Voss's barge rounds the headland. The town's flotilla physically blocks the salvage operation while lawyers Ede summoned arrive with an injunction. Beat: the community as shield.

chapters.title: Voss Counts His Losses
chapters.summary: Voss concedes with unsettling grace, revealing he knew about the letters all along—they were worthless to him, and he wanted to see what Quentin would choose. POV Voss. Beat: the antagonist as dark mirror; Quentin chose differently than Voss once did.

chapters.title: Deliveries
chapters.summary: The letters are distributed; families reunite across old wounds; the dockhand reads his mother's words aloud at the dock. POV ensemble, anchored by Wren watching Quentin hand over the last bundle. Beat: inheritance fulfilled by giving it away.

chapters.title: Home Field
chapters.summary: Epilogue one season later: Quentin flies the same route but now lands home each evening; the hangar holds two planes and three names painted on the wall. Final image: Quentin logging the day in hours, not miles. Beat: arrival, at last, without leaving.
